sources.note: Nothing. Image-only scan; scanned PDF pp. 1-118 and 121-124 (front matter, ch. I-VII, lexicon intro) one page at a time and grepped: no use of 'stress' or 'accent' as a prosodic notion anywhere. Table of contents has chapters on consonants, prosodies (labialization/palatalization), vowels, and ch. VI 'Tone' (pp. 93-101: two contrasting tones H/L, all tone patterns possible on 1-3 syllable words, contour tones = two tones on one syllable, a few treated as intonation); conclusion (p. 104) names word juncture, phrase-level features and intonation as future research. sources.citation: Gravina, Richard. 2014. The Phonology of Proto-Central Chadic. LOT Dissertation Series 375. Utrecht: LOT.
sources.note: Nothing on Bana stress. Sec. 6.5.1 'Bana' (pp. 166-167) summarises Hofmann 1990 (three vowels /ə e a/, syllable-level palatalization prosody, labialized velars); the work explicitly excludes tone and stress from its reconstruction.
